method.description: Same MoonBit release JS AOT artifact, bound SQL and data. Snapshot = existing full SavedState JSON per strict IDB commit. Semantic = materialized column patches (v2, with v1 replay) plus binary side attachments. Pages = full SQLite export, full-buffer 4096-byte comparison and binary dirty pages in the same IDB journal contract; not a lazy pager and not OS-aligned I/O. Both incremental paths compact at 128 records or 4 MiB. Point updates alternate equal-width INTEGER values; batch alternates +/-1 on 16 adjacent rows. Per-call total, preparation and IDB submission+strict-complete recorded; all 7x32 operations retained including compactions. ASCII payload lengths count submitted image/delta bytes, excluding constant generation metadata; --blob stores the same pseudorandom ASCII bytes as BLOB instead of TEXT. Both layouts use two puts per commit. Native typed-result hashes checked after each workload and after replay; page files reopened by native SQLite. CPU run sequentially on one machine, no throttling. Separate fresh Chromium context/page per layout/dataset.
method.memory: Baseline/retained/prepared/after use CDP Runtime.getHeapUsage after forced GC. Used JS heap and backingStorageSize are separate. observedPeak samples without forced GC during a separate untimed 64-update workload at a requested 2ms interval. Its first write forces a full checkpoint to match compaction phase across journal versions; timed workloads keep their natural checkpoint schedule. Timestamps, simultaneous combined bytes, and each probe operation kind/bytes/duration are retained. CDP latency and synchronous work can hide transient peaks. This is a sampled high-water observation, not an exact allocation peak, RSS or IndexedDB service memory. Prepared is paused just before IDB submission. Current engine keeps all rows; pages add a full SQLite buffer.
